reasons.hexweaver: The best parts are the boss presentation (named health bar with phase pips, 'enraged' and 'Vanquished' banners), large crit numbers, loot beams with rarity-coloured item cards, and a full HUD with cooldowns and a minimap. The frames are often cluttered: big translucent spell effects and close-up bloom (frames 1, 3, 12) hide enemies, and only a few orange or red ground telegraphs are visible. Enemies are simple, low-detail models, half the frames show empty streets with no combat, and the art and spell effects look closer to a prototype than a commercial action RPG.
reasons.pyromancer: Strengths: the HUD is complete, with a boss bar that shows phases and named attacks, cooldown numbers on the spell bar, a minimap and a low-health vignette. Loot is handled well too, with rarity-coloured beams, labels and pickup toasts, and red ground telegraphs plus floating CRIT numbers make combat easy to follow. Weaknesses: the visuals are low-poly and blocky, and ember_bolt makes up 75 of 83 casts, so the fire effects look like generic glows and blobs. Enemies are simple stacked-primitive models, the third-person-style camera puts the wizard in the way of the action, and bursts of overlapping numbers and labels make some frames cluttered.
reasons.stormcaller: The boss fight is the high point: a named boss bar with phase labels (PHASE II, ENRAGED) and named attacks (Great Toll, Clapper Sweep) is shown with red ground rings, alongside crit damage numbers, a 'Vanquished' banner, rarity-coloured loot beams and item comparison toasts. Many frames are hard to read, though: big translucent cyan and gold effects block the camera, the spark_lance spam has little visual weight, and the enemies are simple low-poly models in a flat-shaded town with no visible hit-stop or knockback. The second half of the clip is empty walking and loot pickup, and loot is almost all common or uncommon, so it builds little excitement.
reasons.warden: Strengths: the HUD is clear, with a phased boss bar, a 'Phase II' banner, a spell bar with cooldowns and a minimap. Combat has red ground telegraphs, crit/'Vanquished' callouts, rarity-coloured loot toasts and a rare-item light beam, and the enemies are distinct, if low-poly. Weaknesses: a third of the frames show an empty square with no combat, damage numbers overlap into unreadable strings like '31144', some spell effects white out the screen and hide the action, and the flat placeholder-style art falls well short of commercial polish.
